item: Fuel delivery - pump, filter, fuel pressure
evidence: Truck pulls great under load; these components fail under load first. Later proven directly: 12.3:1 commanded and delivered at wide open throttle.

item: Compression, valves, cam timing, phasers stuck in a fixed wrong position
evidence: All worsen under load, and the truck is flawless under road load. The elimination was explicitly noted as NOT covering a phaser or VCT solenoid misbehaving at idle.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Elimination record'; 'Why suspect 3 was previously eliminated'

item: Ignition - spark plugs, coils, boots
evidence: Plugs were replaced with no change; ignition faults bite under load and this truck has none.

item: Engine mounts, harmonic damper, flexplate, driveline, exhaust contact
evidence: Symptom reproduces at a standstill in Park; D and R feel identical to each other, and nothing mechanical moves a tachometer needle.

item: Engine mounts - loss of hydraulic damping
evidence: The D-versus-R test only rules out torque-reaction faults; a mount that has lost its fluid is not direction-dependent, so that test is blind to it. Engine rocks on its mounts at 8-15 Hz at idle; first order at 650 rpm is 10.8 Hz, dead centre of that band. Converter drag in gear preloads the engine and changes the mode.

item: Flexplate / crank pulley / rotational imbalance as a direct driver
evidence: The rpm sweep in Park did not grow continuously with rpm, which is what imbalance driving the cab directly would do.

item: Harmonic balancer (crank pulley damper)
evidence: Twelve years of Jeddah heat degrades the rubber bonding the outer ring to the hub; a failed one produces first-order vibration, which is what the rpm sweep points at. Never inspected. Check concentricity engine-off, then watch it spin at idle with a light or timing light.

item: Contact point - exhaust pipe, A/C line, power steering line, transmission cooler line, wiring loom, heat shield touching frame or cab
evidence: Shifting into gear rotates the engine slightly and a part that merely touches at rest breaks contact. Gives strong in P, gone in D, felt not heard, invisible to every sensor, present since purchase, unaffected by six repairs. Never searched for.

item: Tyres and wheel balance
evidence: Symptom reproduces at a standstill in Park.

item: Driveshaft and U-joints
evidence: Symptom reproduces at a standstill in Park.

item: Oxygen sensors as the ROOT CAUSE of the shake
evidence: The symptom is identical cold, where the PCM runs open loop and ignores the sensors entirely.

item: MAF / air metering calibration error
evidence: Factory airbox and duct, no oiled aftermarket filter, so MAF calibration is as Ford intended.

item: Fuel quality or octane
evidence: Always 95 octane from the same station, and the symptom is utterly constant.

item: Aftermarket PCM tune
evidence: Never tuned; no evidence of prior engine work.

item: Unlearned adaptive memory / young adaptives
evidence: The owner performed a relearn and drove 300 km with no change to the symptom - 'i did relearn and drove 300km before this wipe and it didn't solve it'.

item: Intake manifold gasket disturbed during the injector job
evidence: The manifold was removed and refitted with ZERO change to the symptom.

item: Throttle body carbon
evidence: Removed from the manifold and hand-cleaned properly, with no change. (Corrected from an earlier repo assumption that it had never been cleaned - the owner called that out.)

item: Fuel injectors - flow and spray pattern
evidence: Removed, cleaned and flow-tested on a bench during earlier work.

item: Thermostat / warm-up enrichment
evidence: Thermostat reaches and holds normal temperature (ECT 93-94 C warm, 98 C after three hours idling), so the PCM does exit warm-up enrichment.

item: Coolant intrusion / internal timing-chain-driven water pump
evidence: Coolant level steady, no loss. Standing instruction: if coolant ever disappears with no external leak, check the oil before chasing anything else.

item: Idle air control / low idle speed
evidence: Idle normal at 650-750 rpm warm in Park, and no change with A/C load.

item: External EGR valve stuck or leaking
evidence: This engine has no external EGR valve - the 3.7 Ti-VCT uses twin independent cam phasing for internal EGR through valve overlap. RockAuto's catalogue is consistent: the 2014 3.5L EcoBoost lists an EGR valve control solenoid, the 3.7L does not. Earlier revisions wrongly listed it as a ranked suspect and requested an EGR position PID. [VERIFY against the service manual]
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'There is no external EGR valve on this engine'; CLAUDE.md 'Careful'

item: EVAP purge valve stuck partly open
evidence: Never touched in twelve years. Reported as a very common failure on the 2009-2014 F-150, and Mustang 3.7 sources name stuck-open as THE failure mode of Ford's purge valve. Frequently sets no code. Ranked #1 suspect.

item: EVAP purge as the DRIVER of the rpm oscillation
evidence: Commanded evaporative purge is flat at 40.78 percent, stepping down one LSB at a time (40.78, 40.39, 40.30, 40.00) over about two minutes. A flat command cannot drive an oscillation. Re-confirmed after the valve replacement: the new valve modulates over 10-30 s while the hunt runs at 3-4 s, and five paired windows show no correlation.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test B'; 'It is not driving the rpm hunt'; CLAUDE.md

item: EVAP purge valve as the source of unmetered air at idle
evidence: Learned long term trim slope before the repair (+3.13/+2.34 percent at idle, +0.78 just above idle, 0 percent at 2000 rpm) is the signature of a fixed-size opening. Replacing the valve moved the symptom boundary (shake gone in D and R) and, after a relearning drive, idle trim read -0.78 percent on BOTH banks - the lean bias completely gone. The new valve also modulates 47.06-49.80 percent where the old one sat flat, further evidence the old one was not responding to command.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE LEAK IS CLOSED'; 'PURGE VALVE REPLACED'; CLAUDE.md; [206];[251];[252]

item: A second remaining unmetered-air source
evidence: Argued immediately after the repair because the remaining shake sits in the highest-vacuum condition. Killed by the post-drive idle trim of -0.78 percent on both banks - there is no lean bias left for a second source to explain.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; [207];[251]

item: PCV valve, hose, grommet and elbow
evidence: Ranked #2 suspect for most of the investigation - never inspected, twelve years of Jeddah heat, hard plastic that cracks. Withdrawn without ever being physically tested: after the purge valve replacement and the relearning drive there is no lean bias left at idle for it to explain.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; CLAUDE.md; [251]

item: Brake booster line and check valve
evidence: Never tested. Withdrawn on the same evidence as PCV: idle trim -0.78 percent on both banks with relearned adaptives leaves no lean bias to explain.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; CLAUDE.md

item: Intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, injector O-rings (joints disturbed by earlier work)
evidence: Could not be isolated by unplugging anything, which is where a smoke test would have earned its place. Withdrawn on the post-drive idle trim of -0.78 percent both banks. Noted at the time that they could not be the ORIGINAL cause anyway since the shake predates all repair work.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; CLAUDE.md

item: Smoke test of the intake tract
evidence: Justification reversed twice: not warranted when LTFT read 0 percent and was believed un-learned; justified once LTFT read +2.34 at idle and 0 at load; withdrawn again after the purge valve closed the leak. Never performed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'A smoke test is now justified'; 'The unmetered-air line of inquiry is finished'; [200];[251]

item: Vacuum leak / unmetered air, as a family
evidence: Idle long term trim -0.78 percent on both banks, identical, min = avg = max across three windows, with adaptives fully relearned after a proper drive. The engine no longer runs lean at idle by any amount.

item: VCT solenoid / cam phaser misbehaving at idle
evidence: Ranked #3. Oil pressure is lowest at idle so phaser control authority is weakest exactly there, giving dilution that clears as load and pressure rise. Two things argued against it from the start: VCT faults normally set P0010-P0024 and there have been no codes, and the classic description is rough-cold-smooths-warm while this is identical cold and hot.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Open suspects, ranked'; 'Why suspect 3 was previously eliminated, and why it is back'

item: VCT / cam phasers - live data at idle
evidence: Variable camshaft actual advance #1 reads 0.00 to -0.06 degrees, two adjacent quantisation steps on an axis spanning six hundredths of a degree. The phaser sits parked at rest. Limit acknowledged: intake bank 1 only, one of four phasers.

item: VCT / cam phasers - Mode 06 monitor
evidence: VVT Monitor bank 1 error 0.06 degrees and bank 2 error 0.05 degrees against a 20 degree limit; TIDs $82, $83 and $84 all 0 degrees. The phasers track their commanded target within six hundredths of a degree. Far stronger than the live-data reading.

item: Timing chain stretch
evidence: Reported TSB method (VCT_INT_ACT1 >= +6 degrees at idle indicates a worn chain; more than 5 teeth of tensioner extension confirms with the cover off) recorded but marked [VERIFY - reported in a TSB summary, source document not read]. Never measured. Weakened by the Mode 06 VVT result.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test procedures - VCT solenoid and phasers'; [5]

item: Oil pressure at hot idle below the phaser requirement
evidence: Reported requirement of at least 25 psi for phasers and tensioners, marked [VERIFY]. Mechanical gauge test never performed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Test procedures - VCT solenoid and phasers'

item: Closed-loop fuel control as the source of the idle oscillation
evidence: Short-term fuel trim never leaves plus/minus 1.56 percent, quantised in 0.78 percent steps, session averages -0.92 to -0.17 percent across eight captures. If the fuel loop were hunting STFT would swing plus/minus 10-20 percent in rhythm with rpm.

item: Closed-loop fuel control as the source of the idle oscillation
evidence: REVERSAL of the row above - it was a conceptual error. STFT is the correction applied AROUND the commanded ratio, not the mixture. Fuel/Air commanded equivalence ratio is a square wave 14.41 to 14.86 AFR at 3.4-4 s, measured lambda on both banks follows it, and rpm follows the resulting torque variation. Fuel control is the SOURCE of the oscillation - though the dither itself is deliberate fore/aft catalyst control and looks normal by every measurable property.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'This corrects an earlier claim in this file'; CLAUDE.md; [173] error 10

item: Oxygen sensors as the cause of a slow closed-loop cycle
evidence: The corrections produced are far too small to move the idle 40 rpm; and the sensors have since been measured fast, clean and symmetric on both banks.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The oxygen sensor hypothesis is eliminated'; 'What oscillates with a period of a few seconds - SUPERSEDED'

item: Bank-specific vacuum leak feeding one bank
evidence: Proposed to explain a claimed bank 2 STFT offset of +3.5 percent. Killed when long term trim learned to +3.13 (B1) and +2.34 (B2) - one quantisation step apart, the smallest difference the PID can express.

item: Exhaust leak upstream of the bank 2 oxygen sensor
evidence: Same evidence: two long term trims within one LSB of each other. The mechanism (low pulsating idle exhaust flow drawing fresh air in through a small leak, lean at idle and normal under load, no code) fitted the load curve but had no bank difference left to explain.

item: Bank 2 upstream oxygen sensor bias
evidence: Same evidence, plus the fuel cut test showing bank 2's upstream sensor sweeping 12.33 to 29.38 fast in both directions and Mode 06 giving 0.014 s response against a 0.4 s limit, identical to bank 1.

item: Leaking injector, bank 1
evidence: Deceleration fuel cut: O2S1 air:fuel pegs at 29.38 (top of the PID range) the instant the throttle closes and holds min = avg = max across three consecutive windows from ~1850 rpm to ~850 rpm. Any seepage would put fuel in the air passing through and the reading could not peg. Measured on the engine, in place, under real manifold vacuum.

item: Leaking injector, bank 2
evidence: Same test, same result: O2S5 air:fuel pegged at 29.38 flat, min = avg = max across two windows while rpm fell 1772 to 1381.

item: Fuel arriving from any other source during overrun
evidence: Purge is normally commanded shut during fuel cut, and nothing shows in the trace regardless.

item: Bank 1 upstream oxygen sensor - 'cleaned by unknown method' concern
evidence: Moved 13.49 to 29.38 in a fraction of a second, held perfectly flat for a minute, repeated it. A lazy or contaminated sensor cannot do that. Confirmed by Mode 06 at 0.014 s response against a 0.4 s limit.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'It is also the best oxygen sensor test'; [233];[254]

item: All four oxygen sensors
evidence: Mode 06: upstream B1 and B2 both 0.014 s against a 0.4 s limit (3.5 percent of allowance, identical); downstream 0.792 s and 0.856 s against 10 s; heater currents matched at 2550/2455 mA upstream and 637/652 mA downstream. All PASSED.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'All four oxygen sensors - healthy and matched'; [254]

item: Fuel delivery under load
evidence: The PCM commanded roughly 12.3:1 at wide throttle and the system delivered it, exercising pump, regulator and injectors at high demand.

item: Fuel trims / mixture error as the cause
evidence: Idle long term trim -0.78 percent both banks identical; cruise -1.56 / -0.78 percent; Mode 06 fuel system monitor 0 on both banks against a 0.7969 limit.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE ECU PHASE IS OVER'; CLAUDE.md

item: Throttle plate - commanded and actual
evidence: Both channels dead flat at idle: commanded 1.57 percent with min = max, actual min = max on a 6.2-8.2 degree axis, while rpm swings 40. Re-confirmed after the repair with min = avg = max across eight windows while rpm swung 39-56. Throttle desired vs actual also tracks within 0.27-0.43 degrees on the value reads.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Measured this session'; 'The throttle is still completely static'

item: MAF signal oscillating with rpm
evidence: MAF flat at about 3.01 g/s, plus/minus 1.7 percent, while rpm swings 40. Noted honestly that this is EXPECTED at idle (choked flow through a fixed throttle) and therefore rules an air-path disturbance neither in nor out.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'MAF being flat is expected, not suspicious'

item: Calculated engine load as an independent witness
evidence: It is arithmetic the PCM does on MAF, rpm, baro and intake temperature - with MAF constant and rpm swinging, load must swing. A restatement of data already held, not a witness.

item: Blocked or restricted catalytic converter
evidence: A live suspect from the downstream O2 asymmetry. Absolute load reached 96.47 percent at wide open throttle with MAF at 215.27 g/s rising smoothly and linearly to the 6832 rpm limiter with no plateau. A restriction chokes the engine at high flow and cannot hide from this test.

item: Restricted exhaust
evidence: Same WOT evidence: 96.47 percent absolute load, no MAF plateau to the limiter.

item: Restricted intake, air filter, intake tract
evidence: Same WOT evidence.

item: Poor volumetric efficiency from wear, valve sealing or cam timing
evidence: An engine with a mechanical breathing problem cannot reach 96 percent absolute load. Cross-check: 215 g/s x ~1.4 gives about 301 hp against a 302 hp factory rating [rule of thumb].

item: Bank 1 catalytic converter - reduced oxygen storage
evidence: Bank 1's post-cat narrowband voltage averaged 0.58-0.63 V swinging 0.17-0.82 against bank 2's 0.70-0.72 V swinging 0.30-0.83, meaning bank 1 buffers less of the commanded dither. First thing in the investigation to point at one component on one bank. Explicitly recorded as not condemnable from idle data.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Bank symmetry - upstream identical, downstream not'; [165]

item: Bank 1 catalytic converter - reduced oxygen storage
evidence: Mode 06 catalyst monitor: bank 1 0.3711, bank 2 0.3633 against a 0.8359 limit - both at 44 percent of the failure threshold and within 2 percent of each other. The idle asymmetry was an artefact of reading a swinging narrowband signal at the worst operating point for judging a converter.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The catalyst question is settled'; CLAUDE.md; [254]

item: Both catalytic converters
evidence: Mode 06 values at 44 percent of limit, both PASSED and matched; and their good oxygen storage is what makes the fore/aft control loop SLOW at 3.4-4 s - a degraded converter would make the loop run faster.

item: Single weak cylinder / uneven cylinder contribution
evidence: The last ECU-visible mechanism that could produce a felt idle vibration with no code. Would appear at half engine speed, ~5.5 Hz at this idle, and is what the injector-kill balance test and the accelerometer test were designed to name.

item: Single weak cylinder / uneven cylinder contribution
evidence: Mode 06 per-cylinder misfire (TID $0C): 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 1 with the ten-cycle EWMA (TID $0B) ZERO on all six; manufacturer TIDs $80 and $81 read 0 percent on every cylinder. A genuinely weak cylinder produces tens to hundreds of counts and a non-zero rolling average. The three counts are plausibly the 6832 rpm rev-limiter hits in the same session. Independently supported by the rpm sweep, which showed no worsening between 1000 and 1800 rpm where half-order excitation would sweep into the mount resonance band.

item: Misfire
evidence: Misfire monitor Available/COMPLETED with DTC count 0 at the first live-data read, and Mode 06 per-cylinder counts effectively zero after the drive.

item: Knock / spark retard from detonation
evidence: Knock retard reads 0 degrees on every value read; learned octane -0.6, a small adaptive offset.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Values that close out open questions'; CLAUDE.md

item: Cylinder balance by injector kill (six rpm drops)
evidence: Listed as a physical test throughout; never performed. Largely pre-empted by the Mode 06 per-cylinder result.

item: Alternator has stopped charging
evidence: Battery state of charge ROSE from 88 to 90 percent between sessions and then charging stopped, with [BCM] Vehicle Battery Current falling from 1 A to 0 A and voltage settling to battery level. A failed alternator cannot raise state of charge. This is Ford's smart charging strategy cutting alternator drag once the battery is full.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The charging question is answered'; CLAUDE.md; [183]

item: Alternator diode failure injecting AC ripple into sensor references
evidence: DMM on AC volts across the battery at idle, pass criterion under 0.1 V AC. Deferred at the owner's request ('any thing required multimeter save it and will do it tomorrow') and never performed.

item: Ground voltage drops (battery negative to block, block to chassis, battery negative to chassis)
evidence: DMM on DC mV, idling with loads on, each under 0.1 V. Never performed.

item: Crankshaft position sensor / rpm signal integrity
evidence: The one untested hypothesis that would explain the whole data set: a noisy crank signal would make the PCM BELIEVE rpm is wandering, modulate spark to correct a phantom, and that modulation would make the engine genuinely oscillate. Test by measuring engine speed independently of the PCM - timing-light tach, inductive tach on a plug lead, or the phone accelerometer. Never done.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Untested hypothesis that would explain the whole data set'; CLAUDE.md; [146]

item: Wiring / connector intermittency (wiggle test on crank sensor harness, cam sensors, MAF, coils)
evidence: Idling with the rpm graph visible, flex and tap each connector; any rpm response is the fault. Never performed.

item: Body/network DTCs U0422, U0140, B11D8 as the cause of the vibration
evidence: All three are archive/inactive, they are body-network and restraint codes, and the vibration has been constant since purchase - long before the battery was disconnected. An inactive code cannot produce a continuously present symptom. Their pattern is the signature of a voltage event.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'None of it explains the vibration'

item: Active restraint system fault (RCM B11D8)
evidence: No airbag warning light, confirmed by the owner, so the entry is historical. [VERIFY] Ford's definition of B11D8 and the (14) sub-code were never confirmed - the sources were unreachable.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The restraint entry, on its own account'

item: 6R80 torque converter shudder
evidence: Documented across 2007-2020 F-150 and raised in the first web search, but it only shows up in gear under light throttle at lockup, never at a standstill - so it is easy to separate from the idle shake, which reproduces in Park.

item: Transmission / driveline as the source
evidence: Symptom reproduces at a standstill in Park.

item: Coil boots carbon-tracked, or oil in the spark plug wells
evidence: Top reported fix on 2010-2016 F-150s (Ford TSB 14-0160 cited for boots plus gap check); the profile fits a truck where plugs were changed and the shake stayed. Search-summary source only, page never opened. Never inspected.

item: Spark plug gap incorrect after the plug change
evidence: Recommended re-audit of work already done - out-of-box gap is not guaranteed. Never performed.

item: CMCV / intake runner control flaps (P2004-P2007)
evidence: Raised from search summaries; the strongest documentation seen was for the 5.0L V8 and the failure rate on the 3.7 was not confirmed. No P2004-P2007 codes are present on this truck. Never investigated further.

item: Ford long-block replacement program 14B10
evidence: Summaries say it covers gaseous-fuel-prep engines only; this VIN's engine code M is the flex-fuel 3.7, not a CNG/LPG prep engine. Not verified against the actual bulletin.

item: Oil change / oil viscosity as the fix
evidence: The reported case was rough-when-cold cured by an oil change; this truck is identical cold and hot, so the mechanism cannot be the same. (5W-30 against a 5W-20 spec is still worth correcting at the next change.)

item: Carbon cleaning / Seafoam induction service
evidence: The 3.7 is PORT injected, so valve-back carbon matters far less than on a direct-injected engine; the injectors were already flow-tested and the throttle body properly cleaned.

item: A/C compressor cycling as the cause of the rpm oscillation
evidence: The oscillation is present with A/C off (spans 37, 74, 38, 30, 53 rpm); A/C on roughly doubles the amplitude (64-81 rpm) but does not create it.

item: Cooling fan engagement
evidence: One discrete event in five A/C-off windows: rpm dipped to 606-612, held briefly, then recovered with an overshoot to 680. It has width so it is not a dropped frame. Also offered as one explanation for the rpm refusing to hold at 2000 with coolant at 98 C. Never tested directly.

item: Ethanol content inference (16.08 percent on nominally E0 pump fuel)
evidence: Affects open-loop fuelling only, and the inference depends on the O2 sensors, which were 'cleaned' by an unknown method. Read 16.08 percent in two separate sessions, unchanged. [VERIFY against a second tool] - never done.

item: Barometric pressure reading 4 percent low (97 kPa at sea level) causing the lean bias
evidence: Direction and rough magnitude match the +2.3 to +3.1 percent trim measured at the time, but the actual local pressure at that hour was never checked, and on a MAF-based strategy the baro term is a correction rather than the primary input. Superseded in practice by the load-cell slope, which showed a fixed-size opening rather than a proportional error.

item: MAF reading slightly low (proportional calibration error) as the cause of the lean bias
evidence: A MAF or barometric calibration error is proportional and would put the same value in every load cell. The measured correction faded smoothly with airflow - idle +3.13/+2.34, just above idle +0.78, 2000 rpm 0 - which is the behaviour of a fixed-size opening instead.

item: Normal drift on a twelve-year-old engine as the explanation for the +3 percent lean bias
evidence: Offered as one of four candidates for an even lean bias. Ruled out by the same load-cell slope, and finally by the trim returning to -0.78 percent after the purge valve was replaced.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What replaces it'; 'THE LEAK IS CLOSED'

item: Engine coolant temperature / thermostat
evidence: ECT 93-94 C warm, rising to 98 C after three hours of idling at 36 C ambient - within normal, with the fan expected to cycle around 100-105 C.

item: Bank imbalance in exhaust temperature
evidence: Catalyst temperature Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Bank 2 Sensor 1 read identically (458.9 / 458.9 C, later 459.9 / 459.9 C).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Values that close out open questions'

item: Intake heat soak
evidence: Ambient air temperature 37 C against intake air temperature 38 C after 37 minutes idling - 1 degree apart.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Values that close out open questions'

item: Idle governor limit-cycling as NORMAL behaviour rather than a fault
evidence: The live alternative reading of the whole data set. Every measurable property of the commanded dither looks normal: both upstream sensors respond in 0.014 s against a 0.4 s limit, both catalysts sit at 44 percent of limit (good storage makes the fore/aft loop slow), and plus/minus 1.5 percent commanded AFR is within what many Ford PCMs run. Only a control sample on another 3.7 can settle it.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE READING THIS FORCES'; 'Amplitude - stated honestly'; [259];[260]

item: Whole engine as a running fault (mechanical, electronic and combustion)
evidence: Every test the powertrain computer can run has been run and all passed with margin: per-cylinder misfire, catalysts, all four O2 sensors, cam phasers, fuel system monitor, fuel trims, injector sealing on fuel cut, 96.47 percent absolute load at WOT, 0 degrees knock retard, and no powertrain code ever. An engine-running fault would have shown itself in at least one of them.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'THE ECU PHASE IS OVER'; CLAUDE.md; [255]

item: Vibration transmission path (mounts, isolation, contact) as the remaining cause
evidence: What is left after the ECU phase closed. Invisible to the OBD port by physics: the app's response time is 56-117 ms so it resolves 4-8 Hz at best, while first order at 650 rpm is 10.8 Hz and the firing pulse is 32.5 Hz. Everything from here is hands-on - harmonic balancer, engine mounts, contact point, and the phone accelerometer to name the frequency.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'What remains is vibration and its transmission path'; CLAUDE.md; [255];[264]

item: Whether a fault exists at all (the original framing question)
evidence: Still not settled. The control sample on another 2011-2014 F-150 or Mustang 3.7 at warm idle in Park - the test named from the first night as the one that answers in two minutes what six repairs have not - has never been performed. Ford's stated position on a Mustang 3.7 vibration complaint was that it is normal operation.

item: Phone accelerometer frequency identification of the felt vibration
evidence: The test that addresses the actual complaint. Should name the family: ~10 Hz engine rock on mounts, ~11 Hz rotational imbalance, ~5.5 Hz one cylinder differing, ~33 Hz firing pulse meaning an isolation problem - and, after the Park/Drive finding, also look for a ~0.28 Hz amplitude modulation. Never performed.

item: Mount touch test, engine-rock observation, contact hunt and pry-bar mount unloading
evidence: Four free hands-on tests specified in detail; none reported as performed.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The tests, all free, all hands-on'; [225];[226]

item: Vacuum gauge on the manifold at warm idle
evidence: Not for leaks - trims already exclude those - but for combustion character at a bandwidth OBD cannot reach. Steady 18-22 inHg expected. Never performed.

item: Independent rpm measurement (timing-light tach against the app)
evidence: The direct test of the crank-signal hypothesis. Never performed.

item: Cold start behaviour of the needle breathing and of the commanded dither
evidence: A cold engine runs open loop, so the catalyst dither does not run at all - capturing Engine RPM plus Fuel/Air com. ratio from the first crank would prove or break the causal chain. Also the only way to learn whether the NEEDLE BREATHING (as opposed to the felt shake, which the owner reports is identical cold and hot) is present cold. Never captured.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'The test that separates them, and it is free'; 'What still settles it'; CLAUDE.md

item: Permanent DTCs (Mode 0A)
evidence: The only code history a clear or a battery disconnect cannot destroy. Requested repeatedly, never read - and the KAM wipe performed with the purge valve replacement happened before it was captured.

item: Freeze frame data
evidence: Requested in the field sheet (session E6); never captured, and erased by the KAM wipe.

item: EVAP system leak (tank and canister)
evidence: The Evaporative System monitor is the only one still reading 'Not completed' - it needs fuel-level, temperature and cold-soak conditions not met since the valve was changed. It checks the tank and charcoal canister for vapour leaks, an emissions matter, not the idle question.
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Monitor status since DTC reset'; CLAUDE.md; [266]

item: PCM calibration out of date (a reflash with no parts)
evidence: Quick win #3: read the calibration IDs with f150diag survey and ask a Ford dealer whether a later calibration exists for this VIN. Never done.

item: Upstream HO2S switching rate at 2500 rpm (owed repair, separate from the shake)
evidence: Carried throughout as a separate owed item because the sensors were 'cleaned' by an unknown method. Closed by the deceleration fuel cut (full-range fast sweeps on both banks) and Mode 06 (0.014 s response against a 0.4 s limit, banks identical).
source: docs/f150-diagnosis.md 'Concern: the oxygen sensors'; 'What is now closed'; [233];[238];[254]
